key_insight: The paper shows that retrieval can do more than fetch relevant facts: it can help language models learn which prior solution patterns to reuse when reasoning by analogy. By pairing retrieval with reinforcement fine-tuning, the model is trained to select examples that match the underlying reasoning structure, not just surface similarity.
problem_solved: Traditional RAG relies on lexical or semantic similarity, which often fails on reasoning tasks because similar-looking problems may need different strategies, while differently worded problems can share the same reasoning pattern. This paper addresses how to retrieve training signals that improve reasoning via analogical transfer rather than shallow similarity.
method: Introduce Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RA-RFT) as a post-training framework.
Use retrieval to surface past examples that are useful for reasoning-by-analogy, then optimize the model with reinforcement learning signals.
Train the model to prefer retrieved demonstrations that align with the hidden reasoning pattern of the target task, improving generalization on complex problems.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical way to make RAG systems stronger at multi-step reasoning, not just factual grounding. It could improve performance on tasks where the best help comes from structurally similar examples rather than semantically similar ones.

paper_title: Learning to Reason by Analogy via Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
paper_authors: Zilin Xiao, Qi Ma, Chun-cheng Jason Chen, Xintao Chen, Avinash Atreya
